papers.title: Medium-Term Cognitive Outcome in Patients With CNS Lymphomas Treated With Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy.
papers.reason: The title indicates clinical cognitive monitoring after CAR-T therapy but provides no specific connection to executive-function modelling or multimodal assessment.

papers.title: Mapping the evolution of dual-task paradigms in cognitive aging: A bibliometric analysis of research landscapes and translational applications.
papers.reason: Dual-task paradigms concern divided attention and executive control in aging, but a bibliometric analysis does not itself provide cognitive mechanisms or empirical findings.

papers.title: Cognitive Effects of Cenobamate as Compared to Perampanel: A Cross-Sectional Multicentre Study in 600 Patients.
papers.reason: This large clinical study directly measures executive-function performance and identifies medication burden as a behavioral determinant, although it does not model specific executive processes.

papers.title: Systemic inflammation, gut microbiome composition, and cognitive performance among older Ugandans with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias: A cross-sectional study.
papers.reason: The study relates inflammation and microbiome measures to global MoCA performance rather than specifically examining executive functions or process-level cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Potential association between dementia polygenic risk scores and subjective cognitive burden in a post-COVID cohort: a hypothesis-generating study
papers.reason: The paper uses a small non-validated self-report sample to relate genetic risk to broad subjective cognitive complaints, with executive function only one of several domains.

papers.title: Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Val66Met Polymorphism and Cognitive Outcome after Stroke: A Systematic Review
papers.reason: The title concerns genetic associations with broad post-stroke cognitive outcomes but does not identify a specific focus on planning, working memory, attention, or cognitive control.

papers.title: Insulin resistance–related metabolic burden, white matter microstructure, and cognitive change: the HABS-HD study
papers.reason: The study links tract-level white-matter microstructure to longitudinal executive-function and processing-speed changes, providing neural correlates potentially useful for cognitive modelling.

papers.title: Influence of Curcuma longa extract on cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease: a single-arm, open-label, observational study
papers.reason: The study reports changes in attention, digit span, and working-memory-related performance in MCI, but its single-arm design and ten-participant analysis make the evidence preliminary.

papers.title: Multimodal assessment of NIBS-induced adaptive plasticity in aging prefrontal networks: ERP and cognitive evidence
papers.reason: This paper directly combines executive-function testing with task EEG to characterize prefrontal N2 modulation and behavioral changes following cognitive training and tDCS in older adults.

papers.title: Screening of Cognitive Impairment Biomarkers Based on Machine Learning and SHAP Interpretability Analysis
papers.reason: The study develops an interpretable multimodal clinical and MRI classifier for cognitive impairment, but it relies on global cognitive measures rather than executive tasks, eye tracking, or EEG.

papers.title: Reliability, Validity, and Diagnostic Accuracy of the Persian Six‐Item Cognitive Impairment Test (6‐CIT) in Older Adult Outpatients
papers.reason: This is a useful validation of a brief MCI and dementia screening instrument, but it does not specifically assess executive-function mechanisms or use digital or multimodal biomarkers.
